customize.text: Aila's Notes

...I told a lie, just like Lovia did, and just like my sister did. I said no when Mr. Solovei asked me if I felt any hate.
...But how can I put the hatred in my heart into words? How would someone as kind and sincere as he is ever understand such horrifying malice?
...No. I cannot think this way, and no one needs to know. Mr. Solovei does not need to be troubled with such trivial things. No one is obliged to bear the weight of another's suffering, which they have not experienced. And even if he truly were willing to listen, and even if his kindness were to move him to tears... what would it change? I would only end up bringing needless pain to another tender heart. In the past, the present, and the future, across the countless threads of fate that Lovia once let me glimpse by mistake, the only ones who shed tears for the misfortunes of others are kind souls who ought to be smiling instead. And since the sublunary sphere has always been one where good is repaid with cruelty, the least I could do is spare him a sorrow that does him no good.
...Once upon a time, I despised lies. Yet now, I find myself speaking them with keen intent. Maybe the [...] of the past dozen years or so has been punishment for this very moment...
...But that does not matter anymore. From the noble lady of Salt to the scions of Gurabad's jinni, there have been plenty of instances where the innocent have suffered the gravest of punishments, let alone a sinner as steeped in [...] as I am. If the silvery-white thread has already found its way around my neck, I may as well bear the weight of still more unforgivable sins by myself so that the children who remain untainted may be spared...
...What was born of the Frost Moon must return to it. All the walls, towers, fortresses, and temples must be torn down, save for the great pillar raised here by the Dragonborn, that is, the sacred sanctuary where our ancestors found refuge. Prolonged isolation and seclusion serve only to nourish fleeting ambitions and hollow delusions. Let it be reverence for nature, kindness toward outlanders, and those virtues in which none believe, and not the pride of the dead, which sets our threads apart from theirs. Only then will there never again be another Lovia... or another me.
...Decades from now, a new moon goddess will be born... Oh, the irony of it! Lovia's long and desperate quest was, in the end, for nothing. Even if [...] had borne the sacred heir as foretold, and not the man who abducted my sister... The one who should have been our sovereign would only have created even greater chaos in Snezhnaya. The birth of the new moon had nothing to do with anything she did. She could not even foresee the coming of that maiden, and nor did she know that the holy throne had never truly been broken...
...I do not know if I will live to see that moment, for my own thread is hidden from my sight. But I pray that I will not. Those tainted by sin do not deserve to witness the moon's pure light...
...In any case, people must come to believe that the new moon takes delight only in kindness, friendship, and mutual aid — that no other prayer or sacrifice will ever please our goddess. This is what they must believe, because if they do not, then no matter how noble the ideal, it will only wither and fade into the filth that lies beneath the moon...
...The threads of the gods are too bright for me to follow, and I cannot see where she is headed. But at the very least, the Frostmoon Scions, who have been redeemed in her name, must ensure that the power of choice remains hers alone. No one should ever seek repayment or reward from her, and she must never be molded into the "perfect deity" others wish her to become...
...Daughter of the Frost Moon, maiden of the new moon... May she one day behold the dream of true happiness... and may the Frost Moon never forgive my sins, for I have cursed her name more times than I can count.

customize.text: Letter for Aila

Dear Miss Aila,
I am truly sorry that I was unable to stop Miss Alia in that moment. Yet, it was through her noble sacrifice that we ultimately thwarted Rotwang and prevented the loss of countless lives. Now, I finally understand why she pretended to be my close companion. I hope to speak with you about this in greater detail when next we meet — though perhaps, by then, you will already know more about all this than I.
I shall not presume to judge, nor shall I attempt to alter your opinion of her. But I ask, if nothing else, that you allow me to honor Miss Alia's final wishes by sharing her words with you. She asked that I render all possible support to you (which I surely will. You are my benefactor, after all), and that — I relay this only as she spoke it — she hoped that you would go on to live a life of happiness and freedom.
As for the Arrow of Terpikeraunas you mentioned in your last letter, if it truly holds the power to dispel the pitch-black calamity, and if you are willing to share it with such selflessness, then on behalf of the people of Nod-Krai, please accept my deepest gratitude. Should, as you foresee, Rotwang indeed rise again from the pitch-black filth, then our successors — an order I am considering naming the "Lightkeepers," in honor of the flame you have kindled — will stand ready to vanquish the threat once more, armed with the technology you have so generously gifted us.
We can speak of the details in person whenever you are free. I understand all too well that, after Lovia's passing, the Frostmoon Scions have been left with countless matters demanding your attention.
Yours sincerely,
Solovei

customize.text: About the second "Reed Miller"

The second "Reed Miller" was a woman whose real name I do not know. All I know is that she was a traitor to the Frostmoon Scions, who struck her name from history altogether.
In truth, I have no idea what her connection to Avrelian was. And as for the Frostmoon Scions of five hundred years ago... Well, it was a pretty creepy place to be, judging from the poems I've read.
According to Brahe, the entirety of Hiisi Island was encircled by a golden wall even taller than Mont Esus in Fontaine. So I really have no good explanation for how she could have come to know Avrelian.
And now, the Frostmoon Scions have transformed into something entirely different, so much so that I even wonder if they're too gullible these days.
That's why I told Miss Hidimbi just a few days ago that she was real, real lucky. Had she tried to dupe the Frostmoon Scions of five hundred years ago, she'd probably be with Al-Ahmar by now.
So anyway, after Avrelian was executed, she began donning that silver mask, claiming to be the "master thief Reed Miller who had escaped the gallows."
She molded the Treasure Hoarders into a highly disciplined, quasi-military force that almost resembled a religious order. Her mantra was that no one should place their faith in gods or deities, for it was humanity alone that held the power to save its own.
Strange as it may sound, the best way to describe the Treasure Hoarders of that era might simply be "an irreligious religious order."
Under the name "Reed Miller," she gathered a large group of bandits, and together, they picked the governor's palace in Nod-Krai clean in a single night.
All the countless curios, antiques, Mora, and jewels that they made off with... She gave all of that away to the poor of Nasha Town. This was the very "storm of gold and silver" that the cheap novels so fancifully describe.
And now, in Nod-Krai, the people absolutely revere Miller... But if you ask me, that has nothing to do with Avrelian's dream, the dream that my grandmother believes in so staunchly.
For most of the people living on this land, both his dream and Elysium are as distant as the moon.
Who knows, maybe they're just dreaming of someone like her — someone who'd drop loot from nowhere right into their laps, without them having to lift a finger.

customize.text: Alia

After the Golden City of Hyperborea fell six thousand years ago, its descendants, known as the Frostmoon Scions, began to govern the proliferation of countless subsequent generations by law. This was to continue until the blood, thinned by disaster and exile, was purified into holy seed, and mortal descendants were born as perfect beings, fully one with the world. But when, hundreds of generations later, the girl chosen to bear the sacred heir abandoned her mission for a young officer from Snezhnaya and slit her own throat for her love, her death precipitated the fulfillment of the prophecy, and her child never became the chosen one who would lead the Frostmoon Scions to Elysium. The Archpriestess, Lovia, was unwilling to wait hundreds of years for another child of sufficient purity to be born, so she turned to a lesser branch of the bloodline for spares. The twin sisters born into this lineage were pale shadows of the one they were meant to replace, so Lovia committed an act so profane that even the mistress of the Frost Moon would recoil in horror at the blasphemy, and began feeding the sisters the blood of the Frostmoon Scions from childhood.

Sisters Alia and Aila were born imperfect. In the brief moments between agonies, moments that should have been filled with joy, they huddled together, drawing what little warmth they could from each other. They had never seen their parents, nor had they ever heard the wind whispering through the groves. The two of them had only their grandmother, and the only way they'd seen the world was through the pages of a faded storybook. The worn pages revealed a world they had never seen: a single white bird, a streak of grace, gliding beneath a perfect moon. As they admired the free creatures of the fairy tales, the two children made a promise to each other that one day, the two of them would fly together like the white birds in the vast sky. <color=#ffffffd9>"Since the day we were born, it's always been just the two of us. When the day comes for us to leave, let's live the rest of our lives together."</color> But the older sister, Alia, did not keep her promise and set off alone on a long journey that turned out not to be a flight toward a brighter future, but a fall into a much darker night. When the blessed lady's child, Avrelian, returned to Nod-Krai, not becoming the chosen heir of the Frostmoon Scions, Alia fled with him, leaving Aila alone. From then on, all hope for the birth of the sacred heir fell on the younger sister, and she grew up under the control of the Archpriestess, never forgiving Avrelian. And for the Frostmoon Scions, Alia became a traitor, whose name was erased from history.

customize.text: Reed Miller

After Alia escaped with Avrelian, who had become the great thief Reed Miller, she joined the Treasure Hoarders. When Avrelian was executed in Snezhnaya for his crimes, Alia began donning the silver mask and claiming to be "Master Thief Reed Miller who had escaped the gallows." She molded the Treasure Hoarders into a highly disciplined, quasi-military force that almost resembled a religious order. Her mantra was that no one should place their faith in gods or deities, for it was humanity alone that held the power to save its own. The Treasure Hoarders of that era could be described as "an irreligious religious order." Under the name "Reed Miller," she gathered a large group of bandits, and together, they picked the governor's palace in Nod-Krai clean in a single night. All the countless curios, antiques, Mora, and jewels that they made off with were given by Alia to the poor of Nasha Town. Although the Treasure Hoarders had distanced themselves from Avrelian's dream of Elysium, the great thief Reed Miller came to be revered in Nod-Krai.
On the night Alia robbed Trubetskoy's palace, the governor's adopted son, Brahe, noticed her and fell in love at first sight. He was so captivated by her that he even abandoned his noble life to join the Treasure Hoarders. After the death of his beloved, Brahe adopted the name Reed Miller and continued to rob the rich to help the poor and the people of Nod-Krai. Ten years after Alia's sacrifice, the Treasure Hoarders scattered across the world and began to justify their atrocities against the innocent by citing Reed Miller's words. Because Brahe did not want Reed Miller's name to fade into history, forgotten by all, or their ideals to be twisted by future villains, he decided to let these ideals be buried by history and smother them beneath countless contradictory, absurd, laughable yet irresistible stories, until every trace of meaning was worn away with only a sweeping legend remaining. As long as the tale of the Great Treasure continued to be told, there would always be gamblers dreaming of making a fortune overnight, repeating the name of the "Master Thief Reed Miller" endlessly. In the legends Brahe concocted, Alia became Reed Miller's partner, a beautiful woman named Wagtail.

customize.text: Sacrifice

Over five hundred years ago, the Archpriestess Lovia allied with the monk Rotwang, who had arrived from Snezhnaya. Rotwang sought to use the ideal heir of the Frostmoon Scions to reach the pitch-black Elysium beyond the heavens he had once glimpsed. After the death of the blessed lady, who ended her own life when Rotwang's men tried to capture her, Lovia offered Rotwang the use of a sacred relic of the Frostmoon Scions, the Sampo Mill. The Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb was designed in Hyperborea to reconstruct matter at the subatomic scale, or to transmute matter directly into stable energy. The collaborative control module connected to the device was lost during the fall of Hyperborea and couldn't be replicated with existing technologies. At first, the device was sealed, but generations later, when the Frostmoon Scions lost the knowledge of the Hyperboreans and became a religious community, they began to believe that only the prophesied sacred heir could have the power to rouse the Mill and thus bring forth an Elysium of eternal abundance. Rotwang convinced Avrelian to take the Mill from the Frostmoon Scions, promising to create Elysium together, and that's when Alia met him.

After Avrelian's death, when Alia became the new Reed Miller, a man named Solovei arrived in Nod-Krai and began to interfere with Rotwang and Lovia's plans. Realizing that using the Mill could pose a grave danger, Alia pretended to be Solovei's close friend to gain his trust and traveled with him. When the man decided to renounce his surname, he also wanted to drive away his nightingale, with whom he had arrived from Snezhnaya. But Alia felt sorry for the bird and took it with her. When Professor Rotwang built a heaven-reaching tower in Nod-Krai, named the Pillar of Embla, he intended to use the Sampo Mill to siphon the land's power and, through that tower, ascend to the "Elysium" he believed lay beyond the sky. Had his scheme succeeded, all of Nod-Krai — its soil and every living being upon it — would have become fuel for his ascent. Alia and Solovei did all they could to stop him, but at the time, they were too weak. When they reached the Pillar of Embla, Rotwang was one step away from his goal. Realizing there was no other choice, Alia cast herself into the Sampo Mill and, with her own body, ignited it using her purified blood of the Frostmoon Scions. The nightingale and Alia were drawn into the Mill, and by a twist of fate alone, they came to linger in a seam between time and space. The bird later managed to leave the Pillar of Embla in the form of kuuvahki. Five hundred years after Alia's disappearance, it was found by the Lightkeeper, Illuga, in that form. Alia's sacrifice thwarted the Professor's plans and destroyed him for the first time.

Five hundred years after Alia's death, the Professor began to return for a third time and was finally destined to be destroyed. Teaming up with Illuga, the Traveler and Paimon set out to find the "Silver Lampwick," part of one of the three sacred relics: a sword, a lantern, and a mirror, with which, five hundred years ago, Solovei and Alia's sister, Aila, defeated and sealed Rotwang for the second time in Kipumaki Cliff. The Silver Lampwick could create a barrier protecting against the attacks of the Wild Hunt and, according to legend, was in Alia's possession. Over five centuries, Alia's life became steeped in legends, in which she became a Fae and guardian of the Pillar of Embla. When the Traveler and Illuga cleansed the Pillar of Embla of Abyssal energy, they encountered Alia. She was able to return the Silver Lampwick to them, and, stripped of its magical barriers, the Abyss completely overran the Pillar of Embla. Although Rotwang managed to free himself, the Lightkeeper reassembled the Frostmoon Scions' relic, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, and destroyed the Professor for the third time, forever. In his final moments, Rotwang mistook Alia for Avrelian and attempted to persuade her to bend the power of the Sampo Mill to his will, bringing the Elysium beyond the heavens down to earth. But Alia knew that the world the Professor sought was never Avrelian's dream, and that he had only used her to obtain the Mill.

<color=#ffffffd9>"You might have called me Relya by mistake, but it suits me all the same. I carry his role and legacy, and the name Reed Miller is one I will take without hesitation.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Rauthvangi. Mad monk. 'Professor.' Undying serpent... Your story ends here. I will end it in Reed Miller's name."</color>
